files.xgboost_cht_c3.json: XGBClassifier for sensor_fault_active_cht_c3, native XGBoost JSON dump
files.xgboost_bearing_vibration.json: XGBClassifier for sensor_fault_active_vibration_rms_x_bearing_proxy, native XGBoost JSON dump
files.xgboost_combined_engine.joblib: manifest only -- {'model_1': 'xgboost_cht_c3.json', 'model_2': 'xgboost_bearing_vibration.json'}, not a fitted model object

label_remapping.note: Each channel's labels were remapped to contiguous 0..K-1 IDs before training, dropping classes never observed on that channel -- model outputs are NOT directly the standard SENSOR_FAULT_CLASSES = [NONE, BIAS, DRIFT, NOISE, STUCK, DROPOUT] indices. Apply the inverse map below to XGBoost's predicted class ID before interpreting it.

features.feature_order: SENSOR_COLUMNS + MISSING_FLAG_COLUMNS + ROLLING_FEATURE_COLUMNS + engine_state_col_names -- see ml/training/xgboost_classifier/README.md
features.note: Unlike lstm_rul, this model is row-level (no windowing/forecast_horizon) -- rolling features over a within-run window substitute for sequence context.

training.sample_weight: inverse train-split class frequency, per channel

sensor_fault_active_vibration_rms_x_bear.caveat: Only 486 DROPOUT examples in validation -- a near-perfect score on this few positive examples warrants independent re-verification before trusting it as production-grade; see README.

combined_engine_health_binary.description: NONE-on-both-channels vs any-fault-on-either-channel, both models' outputs combined via a simple AND-of-NONE rule
